metadata.changelog: v1.6.6 (dev27, 2026-10-31, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01): cultural_interpretive.semantic.attribution gains an optional `note` in its schema and `natural_language_fields: ["note"]` — the object is not text, its note is, and only the note carries a language tag (rdf_exporter._Datamodel.natural_language_fields). v1.6.5 (MICRO le traduzioni, 2026-10-29, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, domanda 3): the doubtful qualia, MEASURED. contextual.administrative.intervention_history is prose (a history of conservation interventions) and gains `natural_language: true`. provenance_history, exhibition_history, publication_history and contextual.ownership.ownership_chain are `object_chain` WITHOUT a schema: no field of theirs is declared and no code reads a structure, so what a PropertyNode stores is ONE string (the chain as written) — the whole string is marked. cultural_interpretive.semantic.attribution is an `object` WITH separate fields (attributed_to: an E39 Actor reference, attribution_type: a closed list, confidence: a float): none of them is a note, so nothing is marked — the rule is to mark only the note, and this object has none. Its value today travels as one string ("attributed to Phidias") and leaves untagged; marking it would need a `note` field in its schema, which is E.D.'s to add. inventory_number stays a code. v1.6.4 (MICRO la lingua dei dati, 2026-10-27, decided by E.D. 2026-09-28): cultural_interpretive.iconographic.narrative_content gains `natural_language: true` — its value is prose and leaves in RDF with its language tag (crm:P90_has_value "la guerra di Troia"@it), the language coming from the property node's data.lang, else the study's working language. data_type alone does not say it: inventory_number is a string too, and it is a CODE, so it is not marked and never tagged. No other quale marked: the ones whose value may be prose (intervention_history, attribution, the *_history and ownership_chain object chains) are waiting for E.D. v1.6.3 (MICRO em.ttl nel datamodel, 2026-10-26, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01 — every em: term of em.ttl is cited by a datamodel): epistemic.confidence.confidence_level.mappings gains specialised_alternative 'em:confidenceLevel', the em.ttl literal form of the same scalar, declared and NOT emitted (the exporter keeps crminf:I6_Belief_Value via J5). Mapping text only, no quale changed. v1.6.2: added two descriptive qualia of the stratigraphic unit asked for by the DAI record (iDAI.field Layer, D7/D8) — proposte da Cowork per E.D., 28 set 2026, dalla scheda DAI: `feature_shape` (spatial; the shape in plan or section named with a term, AAT 300056273, E55_Type) and `boundary_distinctness` (material; how sharp the limits are: abrupt / clear / gradual / diffuse, E55_Type, no AAT evident). Both controlled vocabularies with indicative seed values; templates declare their own. v1.6.1: added the spatial qualia `geometry` — the PROXY as a quale. The geometry-without-material of a unit becomes a PropertyNode whose payload is a SemanticShapeNode (has_semantic_shape), so the proxy inherits the paradata chain a lone node could not have, and one proxy can be synthesised from several sources. CIDOC default crmgeo:SP5_Geometric_Place_Expression, flagged `confirm_with: Felicetti` (E36 is the alternative, to be decided together with em:AnnotationRegion). v1.6.0: version realigned to the EM language version (EM 1.6) — supersedes the standalone 4.x line (last was 4.2), so all EM JSON config files now share the 1.6.x scheme. Added optional `rationale` + `example` fields to qualia entries (a plain-language why + a concrete case), shown by the EMStudio vocabulary picker when creating a PropertyNode. Seeded for the temporal qualia (absolute_time_start / absolute_time_end / dating_method); to be filled in for the rest incrementally. Prior (4.x) history: v4.2 added rationale/example scaffolding; v4.1: expanded spatial elevation qualia for pyArchInit us_table quote (all E54_Dimension): elevation_relative, elevation_min_absolute, elevation_max_absolute, elevation_min_relative, elevation_max_relative, elevation_min_usm, elevation_max_usm (the generic 'elevation' = absolute MASL, used by quota_abs). Each pyArchInit quota column maps to its own qualia id so they don't collide on the single-PropertyNode-per-property_name rule. v4.0: verified all v3.0 CIDOC-CRM mappings (correct). Expanded with: volume, area, circumference in dimensional; color, texture, finish, patina, hardness, porosity in material; damage_type, fragility, completeness in state; tool_marks, joining_technique in technical; bounding_box, footprint_area in spatial; duration, terminus_post_quem, terminus_ante_quem, relative_chronology in temporal; ceremonial_function, ritual_function, defensive_function, domestic_function, symbolic_function in telic; school, workshop, period_attribution in stylistic. NEW subcategories: iconographic + semantic under cultural_interpretive (iconographic_subject, narrative_content, iconographic_program, aesthetic_value, religious_significance, monumental_status, attribution). Added provenance_history, exhibition_history, publication_history under administrative; NEW ownership subcategory (current_custodian, ownership_chain). NEW CATEGORY epistemic — meta-qualia central to EM paradata model (confidence_level, certainty_level, uncertainty_factors, methodology_used, validation_method, source_quality, primary_contributor, review_status, last_modified).

qualia.name: Origin Type
qualia.description: Natural or artificial origin

qualia.name: Color
qualia.description: Perceived color of the surface or material; classified by controlled vocabulary (Munsell, Getty AAT) or expressed as RGB/HEX value.

qualia.name: Texture
qualia.description: Tactile or visual surface quality (smooth, rough, granular, polished, etc.).

qualia.name: Boundary Distinctness
qualia.description: How sharply the unit is set off from the units in contact with it — the clarity of its limits as seen in plan or section (sharp, clear, gradual, diffuse). A judgement on the interface, not on the unit's shape (see feature_shape) nor on its material.

mappings.mapping_note: E55_Type as every classificatory quale in this file. No Getty AAT concept is evidently this one: left empty on purpose, not forgotten.

qualia.rationale: Whether a limit is sharp or diffuse is how an excavator says how much to trust the limit itself: a diffuse boundary means the line on the plan is an interpretation, and the relations drawn across it are weaker. Recording schemes ask it separately from colour and texture (iDAI.field `featureBorders`, the 'clarity' of a horizon in soil description), so it needs its own quale. The seed values follow the soil-description scale (abrupt / clear / gradual / diffuse); a template may declare its own vocabulary (iDAI.field: deutlich, diffus, verwaschen… — a list that also mixes in the topography of the boundary: eben, wellig, gezackt).
qualia.example: US 3014: upper boundary clear, lower boundary diffuse into US 3021.

qualia.name: Surface Finish
qualia.description: Final treatment of the surface (matte, glossy, polished, brushed, etc.) distinct from surface_treatment which is the procedure.

qualia.name: Patina
qualia.description: Surface alteration layer formed naturally over time (oxidation, weathering, biofilm) or artificially. Modeled as both an observable feature (state) and the result of a modification event.

qualia.name: Hardness
qualia.description: Mechanical hardness measured on a standard scale (e.g., Mohs for minerals, Vickers for metals).

qualia.name: Porosity
qualia.description: Fraction of void volume in the material (0-100%), relevant for stone, brick, mortar.

qualia.name: Damage Type
qualia.description: Typology of observed damage (cracks, fragmentation, abrasion, erosion, missing parts, biological colonization).

qualia.name: Fragility
qualia.description: Susceptibility of the object/feature to damage; qualitative assessment by conservator.

qualia.name: Completeness
qualia.description: Percentage of the original feature/object that survives. Distinct from integrity (which is overall structural soundness): completeness measures missing material.

qualia.name: Tool Marks
qualia.description: Traces left by specific tools on the surface (chisel marks, saw cuts, hammer impacts). Captures both the type of mark and the inferred tool. Closely related to the WorkingUnit (UL) stratigraphic node.

qualia.name: Joining Technique
qualia.description: Method used to join structural or decorative elements (mortar, clamp, dowel, dovetail, tenon-and-mortise).

qualia.name: Elevation
qualia.description: Height above sea level (absolute / MASL). pyArchInit us_table.quota_abs maps here — it is the absolute single-point elevation.

qualia.name: Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Elevation measured relative to a local site datum (not sea level). pyArchInit us_table.quota_relativa. Distinct from 'elevation' (absolute MASL).

qualia.name: Minimum Absolute Elevation
qualia.description: Lowest absolute elevation (height above sea level) of the element's vertical extent. pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_abs.

qualia.name: Maximum Absolute Elevation
qualia.description: Highest absolute elevation (height above sea level) of the element's vertical extent. pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_abs.

qualia.name: Minimum Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Lowest elevation relative to the local site datum. pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_rel.

qualia.name: Maximum Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Highest elevation relative to the local site datum. pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_rel.

qualia.name: Minimum Elevation (USM)
qualia.description: Lowest recorded elevation of a masonry unit (USM). pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_usm.

qualia.name: Maximum Elevation (USM)
qualia.description: Highest recorded elevation of a masonry unit (USM). pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_usm.

qualia.name: Arrangement
qualia.description: Spatial relationship with other objects

qualia.name: Bounding Box
qualia.description: Axis-aligned bounding volume of the element expressed as min/max coordinates. Useful for spatial indexing and rough collision/containment checks.

qualia.name: Footprint Area
qualia.description: Plan-view area of the element projected on the horizontal plane. Critical for architectural archaeology (rooms, structures, sites).

qualia.name: Geometry (proxy)
qualia.description: The geometry-without-material of a unit: what shape it has and where, without asserting what it is made of. THE PROXY, as a quale. The numbers do not live in the property's value — they live in a SemanticShapeNode reached with has_semantic_shape (convex hulls / spheres inline, or a .glb via its url), so the payload can be a file when it is large and inline when it is small, without changing what the property says.

mappings.mapping_note: DEFAULT, defensible, NOT final. SP5 is CRMgeo's class for the geometric expression of a place, which is what a proxy hull is; the alternative under discussion is E36_Visual_Item (the appearance of a thing) — the same choice being confirmed for em:AnnotationRegion, and the two should be decided together. Whichever wins changes the projection of this qualia type, not the modelling of the proxy as a property.

qualia.rationale: Before EM 1.6.2 the proxy was a SemanticShapeNode hanging off the unit on its own, and a lone node cannot say where it came from: it had no paradata chain, so 'the proxy of US101' could not be traced to a measurement, a photograph or a reprojection. As a property it inherits the chain every other quale has (extractor → combiner → property), which is also what lets ONE proxy be synthesised from several sources — a 3D model plus a historical photograph — instead of one node per source with nothing to join them.
qualia.example: The volume of US101 reconstructed from a photogrammetric mesh and a 1931 photograph: one geometry property, two extractors, a combiner, and a SemanticShape carrying the resulting convex hull.

qualia.name: Feature Shape
qualia.description: The shape of the unit in plan or in section, named with a term (circular, oval, rectangular, U-shaped, V-shaped, irregular…). The DESCRIBED shape, as a word; the measured shape is geometry.

mappings.mapping_note: AAT 300056273 = shape (form attribute). E55_Type as every classificatory quale in this file.

qualia.rationale: The shape of a pit or a deposit is one of the first things written on a context sheet and one of the most used to compare units, long before (and often instead of) a measured geometry. Kept apart from geometry because the two answer different questions: geometry is WHERE and HOW MUCH, with a proxy behind it; feature_shape is a classification an excavator commits to by eye. Seed values are indicative; a template may declare its own vocabulary (iDAI.field `featureForm`: U-förmig, oval, wannenförmig…).
qualia.example: US 3009 (cut): U-shaped in section, oval in plan — two properties, the plane said in the paradata or in the template's field.

qualia.name: Absolute Time — Start
qualia.rationale: The earliest calendar date at which the element's time-span begins (the begin-of-the-begin). Anchors an epoch or unit on the absolute timeline; pair it with Absolute Time — End to bound the span. Negative years = BCE.
qualia.example: -27 — start of the Augustan phase of the sanctuary (27 BCE).

qualia.name: Absolute Time — End
qualia.rationale: The latest calendar date at which the element's time-span ends (the end-of-the-end). Together with the start it delimits the absolute chronology of an epoch or unit. Negative years = BCE.
qualia.example: 476 — end of the Late Antique phase (fall of the Western Roman Empire).

qualia.name: Dating Method
qualia.description: Method used for dating
qualia.rationale: How the chronology was established — records the reliability and paradata behind a date so the reasoning can be judged.
qualia.example: c14 for a hearth dated by radiocarbon; stratigraphy for a wall dated by its position in the sequence.

qualia.name: Duration
qualia.description: Length of the time-span associated with the element (event duration, period span). Distinct from absolute_time_start/end which are anchors: duration is the magnitude.

qualia.name: Terminus Post Quem
qualia.description: Earliest possible date for the element ('not earlier than'). One of the two foundational dating bounds in archaeological chronology.

qualia.name: Terminus Ante Quem
qualia.description: Latest possible date for the element ('not later than'). The companion bound to terminus_post_quem; together they bracket the dating window.

qualia.name: Relative Chronology
qualia.description: Position of the element in a relative sequence (before/after specific reference units), independent of absolute dating. Common when absolute dates are unavailable.

qualia.name: Primary Function
qualia.description: Main intended function of the object

qualia.name: Secondary Functions
qualia.description: Additional or subsidiary functions

qualia.name: Ceremonial Function
qualia.description: Use in non-domestic, non-utilitarian ceremonies (civic processions, banquets, public rituals). Distinct from ritual_function (sacred) and symbolic_function (representational).

qualia.name: Ritual Function
qualia.description: Sacred or religious use of the element (cult activity, offering, burial). Distinct from ceremonial (civic) and symbolic (representational).

qualia.name: Defensive Function
qualia.description: Use in defense or fortification (walls, towers, gates, ditches).

qualia.name: Domestic Function
qualia.description: Use in everyday household life (storage, cooking, sleeping, washing).

qualia.name: Symbolic Function
qualia.description: Representational/symbolic role beyond practical use (status display, identity, narrative). Closely related to iconographic and aesthetic qualia.

qualia.name: Structural Role
qualia.description: Role in the overall structural system

qualia.name: Stress Type
qualia.description: Type of mechanical stress the element is subject to

qualia.name: Load Capacity
qualia.description: Maximum load the element can bear

qualia.name: Stylistic Influences
qualia.description: Cultural or artistic influences

qualia.name: School / Workshop
qualia.description: Production school or workshop attribution (e.g., 'School of Phidias', 'Della Robbia workshop').

qualia.name: Period Attribution
qualia.description: Stylistic period to which the element is attributed (e.g., 'Late Republican', 'Early Imperial'). Distinct from absolute dating: this is the stylistic classification.

iconographic.name: Iconographic Qualia
iconographic.description: Subject matter, narrative content, and iconographic program of the element. Specific to artistic or representational objects.

qualia.name: Iconographic Subject
qualia.description: Primary subject or figure depicted (deity, mythological scene, portrait, allegory).

qualia.name: Narrative Content
qualia.description: Story or scene depicted (Trojan War, biblical narrative, historical episode). Free-text or linked to a thematic concept node.

qualia.name: Iconographic Program
qualia.description: Coherent set of subjects forming a thematic whole (e.g., 'Programma augusteo del Foro di Augusto'). Higher-level than individual subjects.

semantic.name: Semantic Qualia
semantic.description: High-level interpretive qualia: aesthetic judgment, religious significance, monumental status, attribution. These are inherently propositional (model as crminf:I4_Proposition_Set in RDF, not as direct dimensions).

qualia.name: Aesthetic Value
qualia.description: Aesthetic judgment about the element ('beautiful', 'sublime', 'monumental', 'refined'). Inherently subjective; the canonical qualia for the EM 'bello/brutto' interpretive axis.

qualia.name: Religious Significance
qualia.description: Religious or sacred role attributed to the element (cult image, relic, sanctified space).

qualia.name: Monumental Status
qualia.description: Recognition of the element as a monument of cultural significance (national heritage, UNESCO, regional protected).

qualia.name: Attribution
qualia.description: Attribution to a specific maker, patron, or commission (e.g., 'attributed to Phidias', 'commissioned by Augustus'). Modeled as an attribute-assignment event in RDF to carry confidence.

schema.note: optional free text in a natural language: the attribution as the source words it, or its grounds (P3_has_note)

qualia._natural_language_note: 1.6.6 (dev27, E.D. 2026-10-01): the object has separate fields, so only its NOTE is text in a natural language and carries a language tag; attributed_to, attribution_type and confidence are a reference, a closed term and a number. Read by rdf_exporter._Datamodel.natural_language_fields. Measured: no writer stores attribution as an object today (it travels as one string, untagged), so the marker waits for the first that does.

qualia_categories.name: Contextual Qualia
qualia_categories.description: Experimental category for management and administrative information

administrative.name: Administrative Qualia
administrative.description: TODO E.D. — proposal 1, to confirm or replace: Legal, inventory and curatorial record of the element
_description_proposals: Legal, inventory and curatorial record of the element
Legal status, inventory identity and curatorial history of the element. The record a holding institution keeps, as distinct from ownership, which is the chain of who has held it.
administrative._description_todo: This subcategory shipped with no description, so its tooltip was empty in the EMStudio vocabulary picker (the only one of 17). The three proposals above match the register of the sibling subcategories — short noun phrase; the longer one mirrors `ownership`, which already defines itself AGAINST this one ('distinct from administrative qualia which cover legal/inventory aspects'). Pick one, move it into `description`, and delete these two keys.

qualia.name: Inventory Number
qualia.description: Official inventory or catalog number

qualia.name: Legal Status
qualia.description: Legal protection and ownership status

qualia.name: Intervention History
qualia.description: History of conservation interventions

qualia.name: Conservation Status
qualia.description: Current conservation state and needs

qualia.name: Access Conditions
qualia.description: Conditions for access and use

qualia.name: Provenance History
qualia.description: Chain of provenance events for the element: production → ownership transfers → current location. Modeled in RDF as a chain of crm:E10_Transfer_of_Custody and crm:E8_Acquisition events linked to the entity.

qualia.name: Exhibition History
qualia.description: Record of public exhibitions in which the element has appeared. Modeled in RDF as crm:E7_Activity instances with temporal scope.

qualia.name: Publication History
qualia.description: Chain of publications referencing the element. Modeled as crm:E31_Document references via P67_refers_to.

ownership.name: Ownership Qualia
ownership.description: Current and historical ownership / custody of the element. Distinct from administrative qualia which cover legal/inventory aspects: ownership is the chain of who has held the thing.

qualia.name: Current Custodian
qualia.description: Current legal custodian or owner (institution or person) of the element.

qualia.name: Ownership Chain
qualia.description: Historical sequence of custodians/owners. Modeled in RDF as a chain of crm:E8_Acquisition events ordered by time.

qualia_categories.name: Epistemic Qualia
qualia_categories.description: Meta-qualia about how knowledge of a node was constructed: confidence in the assertion, methodology followed, and attribution chain (who said what, validated by whom, when). Central to the Extended Matrix paradata model — every claim in EM carries an epistemic dimension. This category is the explicit machine-readable expression of EM's reasoning chain.

confidence.name: Confidence Qualia
confidence.description: Quantitative and qualitative confidence in assertions about the node

qualia.name: Confidence Level
qualia.description: Numerical confidence in the assertion (0-100%). The EM-canonical scalar for paradata-supported claims. CRM mapping changed 2026-07-10: was E54_Dimension; a confidence is the value a belief is held with, i.e. crminf:I6_Belief_Value (see WP3 coverage analysis G5 / Appendix C). The RDF exporter's qualia-precedence rule types the PropertyNode accordingly.

mappings.specialised_alternative_note: 1.6.3: em:confidenceLevel (em.ttl, xsd:decimal on any E1) is the plain-literal form of the same number, declared for a reader that wants the scalar without the CRMinf belief. NOT emitted: the RDF exporter types the PropertyNode crminf:I6_Belief_Value and links it with J5_holds_to_be (_emit_belief_propositions). Putting it in cidoc_crm's place would be the switch, and is E.D.'s decision.

qualia.name: Certainty Level
qualia.description: Qualitative certainty discrimination, complementary to confidence_level for non-numerical reasoning.

qualia.name: Uncertainty Factors
qualia.description: Factors that reduce certainty about the assertion (partial preservation, missing documentation, conflicting sources).

methodology.name: Methodology Qualia
methodology.description: Methods and procedures used to construct the assertion

qualia.name: Methodology Used
qualia.description: Method or procedure followed to derive the assertion (analytical, comparative, experimental, etc.).

qualia.name: Validation Method
qualia.description: Method used to validate the assertion (peer-review, cross-validation, replication, etc.).

qualia.name: Source Quality
qualia.description: Quality assessment of the sources supporting the assertion.

attribution_chain.name: Attribution Chain Qualia
attribution_chain.description: Provenance of the assertion: who made it, who validated it, when

qualia.name: Primary Contributor
qualia.description: Author/agent (human or AI) who first asserted the claim. Links to AuthorNode (human) or AuthorAINode (AI subclass) via has_author edge.

qualia.name: Review Status
qualia.description: Current review status of the assertion in the paradata workflow.

qualia.name: Last Modified
qualia.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the assertion.
